name: GHOSTWIRE.Encounters.Tables.CyborgSystemCrisis
description:
F15 — the Cyborg death-spiral replacement. A full Cyborg who would enter the dying track enters System Crisis instead: no dying saves, no dying strikes, and magic healing does nothing. Roll 2d6 once, here, for severity.

Optional modifiers: −1 for a soft or scrapheap chassis, +1 for a military or overclocked one.

Reboot: an adjacent ally with Repair, Medicine, or Cybertech — or a Wrench or Medic — spends a maneuver and makes a Power Roll. Brick never field-reboots.

Not F12. Crisis is not the Suppressed / Damaged / Destroyed chrome track applied to the Cyborg as a whole, it is not a Body Integrity debit, and it never deletes an Item. Only the Cascade row touches living Chrome, and it does so through the ordinary chrome track.

results.name: Brick
results.description:
The chassis locks. Every actuator goes rigid, the optics go dark, and the Cyborg is an object. Treat them as unconscious. They can be carried, dragged, or loaded into a van, and nothing at the table brings them back in the field.

Recovery: a Repair Project — goal 60, parts running about half a week of Middle Lifestyle — or a Machine God’s Rite or equivalent named ability. There is no field reboot.

Director: this is the row that ends a runner’s night, not their career. Let the crew decide what carrying them costs.

results.name: Cascade
results.description:
One system takes the surge. Pick one installed living Chrome Item at random: it escalates one step on the chrome damage track — Suppressed → Damaged → Destroyed — stopping at Destroyed. Then resolve the Crisis as Limp-Home.

If the Cyborg has no living Chrome installed, it is Limp-Home with a bane on the reboot roll instead.

Recovery: reboot as Limp-Home, then deal with the chrome on its own terms in downtime.

Director: this is the only row that touches Chrome at all, and it goes through the ordinary chrome track. Crisis is not chrome damage applied to the whole Cyborg.

results.name: Limp-Home
results.description:
Down until somebody reboots them. The chassis is intact but running on a degraded profile.

After the reboot: Stamina equal to the Recoveries spent (minimum 1), speed halved, and a bane on tests until a full respite or a Field Repair clears it.

Recovery: reboot now — an adjacent ally’s maneuver.

Director: the most common result, and the one that keeps a Cyborg in the fight while making the rest of it hurt.

results.name: Soft Reboot
results.description:
Down until rebooted, and nothing broke.

After the reboot: Stamina from Recoveries spent, no lasting bane. The reboot itself costs 1 Recovery.

Recovery: an ally’s maneuver reboot, or a printed self-reboot path if the Cyborg has one and has a Recovery left.

results.name: Failover
results.description:
A redundant core catches it. Spend 1 Recovery, stand with that Stamina, no aftermath. The Cyborg does not go down at all.

Once per respite. A second System Crisis in the same respite is Limp-Home instead, whatever the dice say.

Recovery: the Recovery is the recovery.
